title: Compression
overview: Compression reduces the size of a file so it takes less storage and transmits faster. Paper 1 asks why compression is needed, what separates lossy from lossless methods, which method suits a given file and use, and how different file types are compressed, with run-length encoding (RLE) as the method you must be able to apply and trace.
syllabusPoints: Show understanding of the need for and examples of the use of compression.
Show understanding of lossy and lossless compression and justify the use of a method in a given situation.
Show understanding of how a text file, bitmap image, vector graphic and sound file can be compressed.

definitions.definition: Encoding data so that it uses fewer bits than the original representation.
Compression in which no data are lost, so the original file can be reconstructed exactly.
Compression that permanently removes data judged to be unnecessary, so the original cannot be reconstructed exactly.
A lossless method that replaces a run of identical consecutive values with a single copy of the value and a count of how many times it repeats.
A lossless method that replaces repeated words or patterns with short codes stored in a dictionary.
A lossless method that gives frequently occurring characters shorter bit codes and rarer characters longer codes, using codes with the prefix property.
A lossy technique that removes the parts of a sound or image that human senses are least able to notice.
Original size divided by compressed size; a higher ratio means greater compression.

sections.title: Why compression is needed
content: Uncompressed images, audio and video are very large. Compressing them means less storage space is used, files transfer and download faster, less bandwidth is used on a network, and media can be streamed in real time without long buffering. Compression is used for email attachments, web pages, streaming services, backups and archives.
bullets: Smaller files → faster transmission → lower data costs and less network congestion.
Compression and decompression take processing time, which is the price paid for smaller files.
Both sender and receiver need compatible software to compress and decompress.

sections.title: Lossless and lossy compression
content: Lossless compression finds patterns or redundancy in the data and records them more efficiently; decompressing gives back every original bit. Lossy compression goes further by discarding data, usually detail that people will barely notice, so it achieves much smaller files, but the removed data are lost permanently and quality falls with each extra level of compression.
bullets: Lossless is essential for text, program files, spreadsheets and databases, where one changed bit could corrupt meaning or stop a program working.
Lossy suits photographs, music and video for streaming or the web, where a small loss of quality is acceptable for a large saving.
Once lossy compression has been applied, the discarded data cannot be recovered by decompressing.
Many real formats combine both: a lossy step removes detail, then a lossless step encodes what remains efficiently.

examples.label: Justifying a method
examples.content:
A program's executable file must be sent to users → lossless, because any lost bit would change the instructions and the program might not run.
A holiday photo is uploaded to social media → lossy, because the file becomes much smaller and the loss of fine detail is not noticeable on a phone screen.

sections.title: Run-length encoding (RLE)
content: RLE replaces each run of repeated consecutive values with a count and one copy of the value. It works well on data with long runs, such as simple graphics with large areas of one colour, but can make data with few repeats larger, because every single value now needs a count as well.
bullets: RLE is lossless: expanding each count/value pair gives back the exact original.
In a bitmap, each row of pixels is encoded as runs of colour codes.
In binary, each run is stored as a count followed by the value, e.g. a count byte and then the byte being repeated.
The decompressor must be able to tell a count from a data value, for example by using fixed-size pairs or a flag character that marks where an encoded run starts.

examples.label: RLE on a string
examples.content:
Original: AAAAABBBCCCCCCCCD (17 characters)
Runs: 5 × A, 3 × B, 8 × C, 1 × D
Encoded: 5A 3B 8C 1D (8 characters)
The data have been reduced from 17 to 8 characters.

examples.label: RLE making data larger
examples.content:
Original: ABCDEF (6 characters)
Encoded: 1A 1B 1C 1D 1E 1F (12 characters)
With no repeated runs, RLE doubles the size, which is why it only suits data with long runs.

examples.label: RLE stored in binary
examples.content:
Original bytes: 01000001 repeated 4 times ('AAAA', 32 bits)
Encoded as a count byte then a data byte: 00000100 01000001 (16 bits)
A 1-bit black-and-white row 0001111111000 becomes the runs 3 × 0, 7 × 1, 3 × 0

sections.title: Compressing text files
content: Text must always be compressed losslessly, because losing any character changes the meaning. In Huffman coding, the text is analysed to find how often each character occurs; frequent characters are given short bit codes and rare characters longer ones, instead of every character using a full byte. The codes have the prefix property: no code is the start of another, longer code, so the compressed bit stream can be decoded without ambiguity. Dictionary methods are another approach: repeated words or groups of characters are stored once in a dictionary, and each occurrence is replaced by a short index into it.
bullets: Huffman coding turns a stream of bytes into a stream of bits of different lengths.
The code table (or dictionary) must be stored with the file or known to the decompressor, which adds a small overhead.
The more uneven the character frequencies, or the more often words repeat, the greater the saving.

examples.label: Huffman codes and the prefix property
examples.content:
Codes: e = 10, t = 01, o = 111, h = 110, l = 0001
'tee' → 01 10 10 = 6 bits, compared with 3 × 8 = 24 bits in 8-bit ASCII
Decoding 011010: 01 must be t (no other code starts 01), then 10 = e, 10 = e
Because no code is the prefix of another, there is only one way to split the bits.

sections.title: Compressing bitmap images and vector graphics
content: A bitmap can be compressed losslessly with RLE, which is effective on images with large areas of the same colour. Lossy methods reduce the resolution, or reduce the colour depth by setting up a smaller palette and changing each pixel to the closest colour in it, which works well on photographs where neighbouring pixels are similar. JPEG is the most common lossy format for photographs. A vector graphic is already compact because it stores a drawing list; to compress it further it can be converted to Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), which describes the image in a text-based markup language that compresses well with lossless methods.
bullets: Reducing colour depth or resolution before saving is a form of lossy compression.
Lossy image compression can create visible artefacts such as blockiness or colour banding at high compression levels.
Vector graphics should use lossless compression so that object properties are not altered.

sections.title: Compressing sound files
content: Lossy sound compression uses perceptual coding: it removes sounds outside the range of human hearing, and quieter sounds that are masked by louder sounds at the same time. MP3 works this way and typically cuts a music file by up to about 90%. Another technique uses the fact that successive samples rarely change much: the file stores the differences between samples, using a lower sampling resolution for them. The sampling rate or sampling resolution of the whole recording can also be reduced. Video formats such as MP4 apply similar compression to both sound and pictures. Lossless audio compression exists for situations where perfect quality is needed, such as studio master recordings, but it gives much smaller savings.
bullets: Removing frequencies humans cannot hear reduces size with no audible loss.
Reducing the sampling rate or resolution lowers accuracy, so quality falls noticeably at extreme settings.
Streaming services use lossy compression so music plays without buffering on limited bandwidth.

formulas.label: Compression ratio
formulas.expression: compression ratio = original size ÷ compressed size

formulas.label: Percentage saved
formulas.expression: saving (%) = (original size − compressed size) ÷ original size × 100

comparisonTable.title: Lossless and lossy compression
rows: Perceptual coding (MP3), reducing resolution or colour depth (JPEG)
Text, programs, data files, medical images
Photos, music and video for web or streaming

diagram.title: Choosing a compression method
nodes: Identify the file type and its use
No → lossy, if small quality loss is acceptable

analysisChains.title: Using lossy compression for a music streaming service
steps: Sounds humans cannot hear or will not notice are removed
Less bandwidth is needed, so music starts quickly without buffering
But some detail is lost permanently, which trained listeners may notice
analysisChains.evaluation: For casual listening on phones the saving outweighs the quality loss; a recording studio archiving masters would use lossless compression instead.

analysisChains.title: Applying RLE to an image
steps: Runs of identical pixels are replaced by a count and a colour
Images with large blocks of one colour shrink greatly
The original can be rebuilt exactly because RLE is lossless
But a photograph with few repeated neighbouring pixels may barely shrink or even grow
analysisChains.evaluation: RLE suits simple graphics such as icons and diagrams; photographs are better served by lossy methods.

analysisChains.title: Compressing a text document before emailing it
steps: A lossless dictionary method replaces repeated words with short codes
The attachment becomes smaller and sends faster
The recipient decompresses it and gets back the identical text
The only cost is processing time to compress and decompress
analysisChains.evaluation: Lossy compression would never be acceptable here, because losing characters would change the meaning of the document.

examTips: When justifying a method, name the file type and explain the consequence of losing data for that specific use.
Show RLE as clear count/value pairs and count the characters before and after to prove the saving.
Say 'permanently removes data' for lossy compression; 'reduces quality' alone rarely gets the mark.
Describe a specific technique for each file type: Huffman or dictionary coding for text, RLE or colour reduction for images, conversion to SVG for vectors, perceptual coding for sound.
commonMistakes: Saying lossy data can be recovered when the file is decompressed.
Recommending lossy compression for text, program code or spreadsheets.
Assuming RLE always reduces file size; it can increase it when there are few runs.
Describing compression only as 'making the file smaller' without explaining how.
Confusing compression with encryption; compression reduces size, encryption protects confidentiality.

quickRecall.question: Give two reasons for compressing files.
quickRecall.answer: Any two of: less storage space, faster transmission or download, less bandwidth used, allows real-time streaming.

quickRecall.question: What is the key difference between lossless and lossy compression?
quickRecall.answer: Lossless allows the original to be reconstructed exactly; lossy permanently removes data.

quickRecall.question: Why must text files use lossless compression?
quickRecall.answer: Losing any character would change the content and meaning of the text.

quickRecall.question: What is perceptual coding?
quickRecall.answer: Lossy sound compression that removes sounds humans cannot hear or would not notice, such as quiet sounds masked by louder ones.

quickRecall.question: What is the prefix property in Huffman coding, and why does it matter?
quickRecall.answer: No code is the start of another code, so the compressed bit stream can be decoded in only one way.

quickRecall.question: When does RLE work badly?
quickRecall.answer: When the data contain few consecutive repeated values, because each value needs a count too and the file may grow.

quickRecall.question: How can a bitmap be compressed with a lossy method?
quickRecall.answer: Reduce the resolution or colour depth, or group similar colours together and store them as one colour.
